blocks.content:
I still remember standing in Delhi during winter mornings, feeling the heavy air around me. The fog was not just fog — it was smoke. The Air Quality Index crossed dangerous levels, and breathing itself felt difficult.

Like millions of people living in North India, I experienced the impact of stubble burning (Parali burning) every year. But instead of only complaining about pollution, one question stayed in my mind:
Can a student like me actually help solve this problem?
That question became the beginning of my project — Stubble Solution.
🌍 The Problem That Needed Urgent Attention
Every year after harvesting crops like rice and wheat, farmers face a serious challenge. They must prepare fields quickly for the next crop. Farmers generally have two options:

• Manually remove crop residue (time-consuming and expensive)
  • Burn the residue — the fastest but most harmful method
Most farmers choose burning because they lack time, machinery, or affordable alternatives. The result?

• Massive smoke emissions
  • Dangerous PM2.5 particles
  • Toxic gases spreading across cities
  • Severe winter pollution in Delhi and Northern India
  • Respiratory problems for millions of people
This problem doesn't affect only India — it exists worldwide wherever large-scale farming happens. I realized this wasn’t just an agricultural issue. It was a health crisis.
💡 How I Got the Idea

Being from Delhi, I personally experienced pollution every winter. I saw elderly people struggling to breathe, children wearing masks, and news channels constantly discussing AQI emergencies.

Instead of blaming farmers, I tried to understand their reality. Farmers burn stubble because they need a fast solution. So my idea became clear:
👉 What if burning cannot be stopped immediately… but pollution from burning can be reduced drastically?
🏫 My Journey Began — School Level Exhibition

My journey started at Rajkiya Pratibha Vikas Vidyalaya Yamuna Vihar. Our guide teacher, Ashutosh Sharma, encouraged us to participate in a science exhibition supported by institutions like NCERT, SCERT Delhi, and NITI Aayog. I worked on defining the problem, researching chemistry applications, and designing the concept. When our project secured 1st position at school level, it was the first moment I felt: Maybe this idea truly has potential. Our principal, Harish Kumar, motivated us to improve the model further.
🧪 Zonal Level — Facing Real Competition

The zonal competition brought together many reputed schools. Standing before judges and large audiences was intimidating. But when I explained the farmer challenges, chemical reaction logic, and environmental impact, the judges appreciated the practicality of the solution. Our project advanced again, building my confidence as a presenter and innovator.
🏆 District Level — Competing with Top Schools

The district round took place at GBSSS Surajmal Vihar. Competition level increased drastically. Students from elite private schools presented advanced models. Honestly, I felt nervous. But I focused on one thing: clarity over complexity. After intense questioning by judges, our project achieved First Position again. That victory proved that strong ideas matter more than expensive models.
🌟 State Level — Learning Under Pressure

The state-level exhibition was massive. Hundreds of projects, experienced judges, and limited evaluation time. For a moment, I thought everything was over when judges had only 3 minutes left for us. I delivered the entire explanation in crisp, powerful points. We secured 3rd Position and were selected for National Level participation.
🇮🇳 National Level — Rashtriya Bal Vaigyanik Pradarshani 2025

Our project was officially selected for Rashtriya Bal Vaigyanik Pradarshani 2025, hosted at RIE Bhopal. My teammate Samyak Jain and I travelled to Bhopal—my first long academic journey representing my school nationally. Presenting my innovation at the national stage was life-changing.
⚙️ Technical Explanation — How My Stubble Solution Works
My innovation combines chemical emission reduction and biological decomposition.
Phase 1 — Pre-Treatment Spray

A decomposition solution containing ammonium sulfate, magnesium sulfate, calcium carbonate, phosphoric compounds, and enzyme boosters (cellulase & laccase). This softens crop residue and accelerates microbial breakdown.
Phase 2 — Pollution Control Tablet

• Calcium Oxide — captures acidic gases
  • Potassium Carbonate — catalytic oxidation
  • Iron Oxide — improves combustion efficiency
  • Ammonium Bicarbonate — reduces NOx emissions
  • Magnesium Oxide — VOC breakdown
  • Urea & Calcium Carbonate — neutralization reactions
👉 Result: Cleaner burning with drastically reduced toxic emissions.
Application Process

1. Spray decomposition solution on stubble.
  2. Allow overnight reaction.
  3. Apply tablet powder before controlled burning.
  4. Pollutants reduce significantly during combustion.
🌿 Results & Environmental Impact

• Significant reduction in harmful gases
  • Lower smoke density
  • Improved air quality impact
  • Faster residue breakdown
  • Farmer-friendly implementation
🚧 Challenges I Faced

This was not an easy project. Major challenges included explaining complex chemistry to non-technical audiences, designing affordable solutions, and presenting confidently under pressure. I learned that innovation is not only about science — it is also about communication and psychology.
🎓 What I Learned From This Journey

• Real innovation starts from real problems
  • Students can contribute to national issues
  • Confidence grows through action
  • Failure fear disappears when purpose becomes bigger
🚀 Future Scope of Stubble Solution

Future improvements can include large-scale field testing, collaboration with agricultural universities, and eco-friendly commercialization. My goal is to transform this student project into a real-world environmental solution.
💭 Personal Reflection
Innovation doesn’t begin in laboratories. It begins when someone refuses to ignore a problem.
❓ SEO FAQ Section

What is stubble burning? Stubble burning is the practice of burning leftover crop residue after harvesting to quickly prepare fields for the next crop cycle.

Why is stubble burning harmful? It releases particulate matter, toxic gases, and smoke that significantly worsen air quality.

What is Ayush Paul’s Stubble Solution? It is a chemical pre-treatment and emission-reduction tablet designed to reduce pollution released during crop residue burning.
